pr_title: driver: serial: uart_stm32: Calculate suitable PRESCALER value for lpuart
pr_body:
Current driver set a fixed prescaler value for the lpuart that caused certain baudrate configurations to fail due to LPUARTDIV overflow the LPUART_BRR register.


This PR attempt to calculate a suitable PRESCALER for the selected baudrate, throws error and set the closest possible PRESCALER value if it couldn't get an optimal one.

fixes #39608

issue_context.title: stm32: lpuart: 9600 baudrate doesn't work
issue_context.body:
`lpuart1` won't work when it is set to 9600 baudrate on `nucleo_g0b1re` board, in fact it will not work for anything below ~15k baudrate by calculation.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1563974/138208934-bd723674-7966-494c-ae90-cfcd360355be.png)

The `LPUARTDIV` based on the formula above is ~1,706,666, which doesn't fit into a 20bit `BRR` register and was truncated into 658,091 instead after the `LPUART_BRR_MASK` mask, see pictures below.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1563974/138209144-748cdaf2-1d06-49e7-b136-429ad2ed44b5.png)


![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1563974/138208686-2e4ae063-2a4b-4359-b44c-351b319ac169.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1563974/138208843-3c6efb67-7dac-42ca-8d84-f72b3495feb0.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1563974/138208712-f3b889d7-b20c-4ca2-85bf-20101334fd77.png)

review_comments: If there is no way to find a prescaler that allows to match the expected baud rate, user needs to review his application settings. Computing an approx baudrate feels useless to me.

> Computing an approx baudrate feels useless to me.

I agree

@ABOSTM @erwango @FRASTM
I saw that some socs do not have `USART_PRESC_PRESCALER` (stm32l0xx), so this second case here is to make sure that if `LPUARTDIV` happens to exceed the boundary for the `clock_rate` + `baud_rate` combo, at least it wont fail silently
